items.q: Ē quot foribus iānua vīllae cōnstat?
items.en: Of how many leaves does the villa's door consist?
items.hint: a number in the ablative after 'ē'

items.en: Where is the threshold?
items.hint: ablative after 'sub' (under ...)

items.q: Quōmodo appellātur servus quī forēs cūstōdit?
items.en: What is the slave called who guards the door?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (a name)

items.q: Quid facit is quī vīllam intrāre vult?
items.en: What does a person do who wants to enter the villa?
items.hint: verbs with an accusative object (knocks ... and waits ...)

items.en: What is the doorkeeper's dog like?
items.hint: a comparison with 'tam ... quam' (as ... as a wolf)

items.q: Cūr necesse est canem catēnā vincīre?
items.en: Why is it necessary to chain the dog?
items.hint: a reason: it is as ... as a wolf (adjective in the nominative)

items.q: Unde facta est catēna quā canis vincītur?
items.en: What is the chain that binds the dog made of?
items.hint: ablative after 'ex' (out of ...)

items.q: Uter ānulus pulchrior est, aureus an ferreus?
items.en: Which of the two rings is more beautiful, the gold one or the iron one?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative (agreeing with 'ānulus')

items.q: Ē quā māteriā forēs factae sunt?
items.en: What material are the door-leaves made of?
items.hint: ablative after 'ē' (out of ...)

items.en: Who is the god of smiths?
items.hint: a name in the nominative

items.en: What is the doorkeeper doing again already?
items.hint: a verb, 3rd person singular

items.en: Who guards the door while the doorkeeper sleeps?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the subject)

items.en: Who is a letter-carrier?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative with a relative clause

items.en: With what does the letter-carrier knock on the door?
items.hint: a noun in the ablative of means (with a ...)

items.en: How is the sleeping doorkeeper woken?
items.hint: an ablative absolute (with the dog ...)

items.en: Has the letter-carrier come to attack the villa?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'num' expects 'no'

items.en: When will the letter-carrier answer everything?
items.hint: an adverb of time

items.en: What is the letter-carrier's name?
items.hint: a name in the nominative

items.q: Cūr vōx tabellāriī difficilis est audītū?
items.en: Why is the letter-carrier's voice hard to hear?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quod' (the door is between them)

items.en: Where does Tlepolemus come from?
items.hint: a town name in the ablative (place from which, no preposition)

items.q: Quid erus hāc hōrā facere solet?
items.en: What does the master usually do at this hour?
items.hint: a supine with 'īre' (to go to ...)

items.en: Who is Tlepolemus?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative

items.q: Ubi Tlēpolemus stat, cum iānitor forēs aperit?
items.en: Where is Tlepolemus standing when the doorkeeper opens the door?
items.hint: an adverb of place (outside) with 'in' + ablative

items.q: Dē quō iānitor hominem intrantem monet?
items.en: About what does the doorkeeper warn the man coming in?
items.hint: ablative after 'dē' (about ...)

items.q: Cūr nōn opus est Tlēpolemum dē cane monēre?
items.en: Why is there no need to warn Tlepolemus about the dog?
items.hint: a reason: he knows how to ... (infinitive with 'scit')

items.en: Does the picture of the dog frighten the letter-carrier?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'num' expects 'no'

items.en: What does the dog seize with its teeth?
items.hint: a noun in the accusative (the object)

items.en: In what state does the letter-carrier back out of the doorway?
items.hint: a present participle with an ablative (trembling in his whole ...)

items.q: Cūr Tlēpolemus tremit, ut ipse dīcit?
items.en: Why is Tlepolemus trembling, as he himself says?
items.hint: accusative after 'propter' (because of ...)

items.en: What does the letter-carrier think?
items.hint: an accusative with a perfect passive infinitive (that the dog was ...)

items.en: Who broke the chain?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the subject)

items.q: Crēditne Tlēpolemus canem catēnam ferream rumpere posse?
items.en: Does Tlepolemus believe a dog can break an iron chain?
items.hint: a yes/no answer (he does not)

items.en: What was the dog able to tear?
items.hint: a noun in the accusative (the object)

items.q: Crēditne iānitor pallium nūper ēmptum esse?
items.en: Does the doorkeeper believe the cloak was bought recently?
items.hint: a yes/no answer (he does not)

items.en: Do letter-carriers carry gold?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'num' expects 'no'

items.en: What do letter-carriers carry?
items.hint: a noun in the accusative plural (the object)

items.en: To whom is Tlepolemus bringing a letter?
items.hint: accusative after 'ad' (to ...)

items.q: Quis tabellārium forās pepulit, ut iānitor dīcit?
items.en: Who drove the letter-carrier out, according to the doorkeeper?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the subject)

items.en: When does the letter-carrier finally come in?
items.hint: an ablative absolute (with the dog ...)

items.en: Where does the doorkeeper take the letter?
items.hint: accusative after 'in' / 'ad' (motion towards)
